title: Cutoff elastic-reflection collision measure and gain

items.title: Cutoff elastic-reflection collision measure and gain
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Under this assumption Lebesgue measure is the completion of Borel measure ([[cor-lebesgue-sigma-algebra-is-the-completion-of-borel-lebesgue-measure]]), and every Lebesgue-measurable integrable class has a Borel representative ([[thm-completion-measurable-functions-have-base-measurable-representatives]]). Write $\lambda_3$ for Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^3$ ([[def-lebesgue-measure-and-the-lebesgue-sigma-algebra]]). Fix a positive reference speed $v_0>0$, and put $w_0(v)=1+|v|^2/v_0^2$. Let $X$ be the real vector space of equivalence classes modulo $\lambda_3$-almost-everywhere equality of measurable functions $f:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ with

$$\|f\|_{1,w_0}:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}w_0(v)|f(v)|\,d\lambda_3(v)<\infty.$$

Let $S^2=\{n\in\mathbb R^3:|n|=1\}$. For a Borel set $E\subseteq S^2$, define the normalized finite angular measure

$$\sigma(E):=\frac1{4\pi}\int_0^\pi\int_0^{2\pi}\mathbf 1_E(\sin\theta\cos\phi,\sin\theta\sin\phi,\cos\theta)\sin\theta\,d\phi\,d\theta.$$

For $v,w\in\mathbb R^3$ and $n\in S^2$, define the postcollision velocities

$$v'=v-((v-w)\cdot n)n,\qquad w'=w+((v-w)\cdot n)n.$$

The collision-parameter measure is $d\mu=d\lambda_3(v)\,d\lambda_3(w)\,d\sigma(n)$ on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3\times S^2$. Its angular factor is finite and normalized; there is no singular angular weight. For $f,g\in X$, choose Borel representatives and define the gain $\mathcal G(f,g)$ by the almost-everywhere integral

$$\mathcal G(f,g)(v):=\int_{\mathbb R^3\times S^2} f(v')g(w')\,d\lambda_3(w)\,d\sigma(n).$$

The value on any exceptional null set is immaterial because the output is an equivalence class. The next item proves that this definition is independent of the representatives, maps $X\times X$ to $X$, and has the stated collision and moment identities.

references.title: R. Fitzpatrick, Plasma Physics, Boltzmann H-Theorem

items.title: Well-defined elastic reflection gain and collision identities
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal G$, $v'$, $w'$, $X$, $w_0$, and $\mu$ be as in [[def-csm-dk-reflection-collision-gain]]. For $f,g\in X$, the gain is independent of the chosen Borel representatives, is bilinear, and satisfies

$$\|\mathcal G(f,g)\|_{1,w_0}\le 2\|f\|_{1,w_0}\|g\|_{1,w_0}.$$

For $f\ge0$ with finite mass $M=\int f\,dv$ and finite second moment, it also satisfies

$$\int\mathcal G(f,f)\,dv=M^2,\qquad \int v\mathcal G(f,f)\,dv=M\int vf\,dv,\qquad \int |v|^2\mathcal G(f,f)\,dv=M\int |v|^2f\,dv.$$

If $M=1$, set $A=f(v)f(w)$, $B=f(v')f(w')$, and $\Delta\varphi=\varphi(v)+\varphi(w)-\varphi(v')-\varphi(w')$. For every measurable test $\varphi$ for which the displayed integrals are absolutely convergent,

$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}\varphi(v)\bigl(\mathcal G(f,f)(v)-f(v)\bigr)\,dv=\frac14\int (B-A)\Delta\varphi\,d\mu.$$

For each fixed $n$, the map $(v,w)\mapsto(v',w')$ is a linear orthogonal involution, preserves $v+w$ and $|v|^2+|w|^2$, and has Jacobian determinant of absolute value one. The angular measure has full support, hence the product parameter measure $\mu$ has full support on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3\times S^2$. Every pair $(v,w)$ and $(\widetilde v,\widetilde w)$ with the same momentum and squared-speed sum is related by one such reflection.

references.title: R. Fitzpatrick, Plasma Physics, Boltzmann H-Theorem

items.title: Kinetic density, velocity, covariance stress and heat flux
items.statement:
Use the velocity space $\mathbb R^3$ and Lebesgue measure $dv$ fixed by [[def-csm-dk-reflection-collision-gain]]. Let $\Omega=\prod_{j=1}^3(\mathbb R/L_j\mathbb Z)$ be a flat periodic spatial domain with periods $L_j>0$ (in metres in the physical interpretation), and let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open time interval. Let $F:\Omega\times\mathbb R^3\times I\to[0,\infty)$ be a measurable number density in position and velocity. At each $(r,t)$ where the integrals below are finite, assume $0<n(r,t):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}F(r,v,t)\,dv<\infty$ and $\int |v|^3F(r,v,t)\,dv<\infty$. Fix a particle mass $m>0$ in kilograms, with number count dimensionless. In SI, $F$ has units $\mathrm{m}^{-3}(\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}})^{-3}$.

Define $(x\otimes y)_{ij}=x_i y_j$, $\nabla_r\cdot T$ by $(\nabla_r\cdot T)_i=\sum_j\partial_{r_j}T_{ij}$, and $A:B=\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}B_{ij}$. Define the number density $n$, mass density $\rho=mn$, mean velocity $u=n^{-1}\int vF\,dv$, kinetic covariance momentum flux

$$\Pi=m\int_{\mathbb R^3}(v-u)\otimes(v-u)F\,dv,$$

internal kinetic-energy density $e=\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}\Pi$, and heat-flux vector

$$q=\frac m2\int_{\mathbb R^3}|v-u|^2(v-u)F\,dv.$$

Their SI units are respectively $\mathrm{m}^{-3}$, $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, pascals, $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, and $\mathrm{J\,m^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$. The tensor $\Pi$ is symmetric because each integrand $(v-u)\otimes(v-u)$ is symmetric, and it is positive semidefinite because for every $\xi\in\mathbb R^3$, $\xi^{\mathsf T}\Pi\xi=m\int[\xi\cdot(v-u)]^2F\,dv\ge0$. It is the kinetic momentum-flux covariance; in the balance law below it enters with a plus sign, while a continuum tensile-stress variable defined from it would be $-\Pi$.

references.title: R. Fitzpatrick, Plasma Physics, Boltzmann H-Theorem

items.title: Selected phenomenological cutoff collision model
items.statement:
For this selected model, an identical classical particle is nonrelativistic in the explicit sense that its velocity is a vector $v\in\mathbb R^3$ and its kinetic energy is the Newtonian scalar $m|v|^2/2$. The mass $m>0$ is a primitive model parameter in kilograms. At time $t\ge0$, $f_t(v)$ is the probability density of velocity for a randomly selected particle with respect to Lebesgue measure $dv$; it is nonnegative, normalized by $\int f_t\,dv=1$, and therefore has SI units $(\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}})^{-3}$. Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the completed Lebesgue measure used by the mathematical gain definition ([[def-countable-choice]]). A positive speed $v_0$ in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ is a reference scale used only to make the logarithm in the one-particle information functional dimensionless. The Boltzmann constant $k_B>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ is a primitive conversion factor when that functional is assigned entropy units.

Adopt the spatially homogeneous kinetic equation

$$\partial_t f_t(v)=\lambda\bigl(\mathcal G(f_t,f_t)(v)-f_t(v)\bigr),\qquad \lambda>0,$$

where $\mathcal G$ and the elastic reflection $(v,w)\mapsto(v',w')$ are exactly those of [[def-csm-dk-reflection-collision-gain]] and [[lem-csm-dk-reflection-measure-and-gain-identities]]. The angular measure is the finite normalized area law specified there, and $\lambda$ is a prescribed rate in $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$, independent of relative speed; it is not a measured cross-section or a derived microscopic frequency. The selected incoming pair law is $f(v)f(w)\,dv\,dw$, and the gain uses the corresponding product $f(v')f(w')$ after reflection. This factorized independent-pair closure is adopted here; it is not deduced from reversible many-particle mechanics or from a molecular-chaos theorem. The mathematical existence and regularity claims are separate from this physical adoption.

The model's global mild evolution and its finite-energy hypotheses are mathematical claims treated separately from this physical adoption. This postulate makes no claim of a hard-sphere Boltzmann–Grad limit, generic gas applicability, spatially inhomogeneous PDE well-posedness, a hydrodynamic limit, or observed entropy increase.

references.title: David Tong, Kinetic Theory, Part 2
references.locator: §2.2.1–§2.2.3, printed pp. 20–32: kinetic collision equation, molecular-chaos closure, elastic collision kinematics and scattering assumptions.

references.title: R. Fitzpatrick, Plasma Physics, Boltzmann H-Theorem
references.locator: Equations (3.123)–(3.144): homogeneous collision model, H functional and Maxwellian detailed-balance discussion.

items.physical_scope: An adopted spatially homogeneous one-particle velocity-density model for identical nonrelativistic particles with a finite normalized angular reflection law and prescribed collision rate. It is not derived from finite-particle mechanics, a hard-sphere Boltzmann–Grad limit, or a general hydrodynamic limit.

items.title: Regularity and invariance of the cutoff Gaussian-mixture class
items.statement:
Fix $u\in\mathbb R^3$ and positive velocity-squared parameters $0<a<b$ (in a physical interpretation, both have units $(\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}})^2$). Let

$$K_{a,b}:=\{\Sigma\in\mathbb R^{3\times3}:\Sigma=\Sigma^{\mathsf T},\ aI\le\Sigma\le bI\},$$

where the matrix inequalities mean $a|z|^2\le z^{\mathsf T}\Sigma z\le b|z|^2$ for every $z\in\mathbb R^3$. For $\Sigma\in K_{a,b}$, define the normalized Gaussian density

$$\gamma_{\Sigma,u}(v):=(2\pi)^{-3/2}(\det\Sigma)^{-1/2}\exp\!\left(-\tfrac12(v-u)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma^{-1}(v-u)\right).$$

Let $\mathcal M_{u,a,b}$ be the closure in the weighted space $X$ of all finite convex mixtures $\sum_{j=1}^N\alpha_j\gamma_{\Sigma_j,u}$ with $\Sigma_j\in K_{a,b}$, $\alpha_j\ge0$, and $\sum_j\alpha_j=1$. Then:

1. Every $f\in\mathcal M_{u,a,b}$ has a $C^\infty$ representative satisfying

$$ (2\pi b)^{-3/2}e^{-|v-u|^2/(2a)}\le f(v)\le(2\pi a)^{-3/2}e^{-|v-u|^2/(2b)}.$$

For every multi-index $\alpha$, there is a finite constant $C_{\alpha,a,b}$, depending only on $\alpha,a,b$ and not on $f$, such that

$$|\partial^\alpha f(v)|\le C_{\alpha,a,b}(1+|v-u|^{|\alpha|})e^{-|v-u|^2/(2b)}.$$

The common derivative bounds imply that every sequence in $\mathcal M_{u,a,b}$ has a subsequence converging locally uniformly together with all velocity derivatives.

2. The gain in [[def-csm-dk-reflection-collision-gain]] maps this class into itself: $\mathcal G(f,g)\in\mathcal M_{u,a,b}$ whenever $f,g\in\mathcal M_{u,a,b}$.

references.title: R. Fitzpatrick, Plasma Physics, Boltzmann H-Theorem

items.title: Exact kinetic moment balances and unclosed fluxes
items.statement:
Let $\Omega=\prod_{j=1}^3(\mathbb R/L_j\mathbb Z)$ with $L_j>0$, let $I\subset\mathbb R$ be open, and fix $m>0$. Let $F:\Omega\times\mathbb R^3\times I\to[0,\infty)$ be $C^1$, with $n(r,t)=\int F(r,v,t)\,dv>0$. For every compact $J\subset I$, assume some $C_J<\infty$ and $N>6$ satisfy

$$|F|+|\partial_tF|+|\nabla_rF|+|\nabla_vF|\le C_J(1+|v|)^{-N}\qquad(t\in J).$$

Let $a:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be $C^1$ and independent of $v$. Let $Q(r,\cdot,t)$ be measurable with $\int(1+|v|^2)|Q|\,dv<\infty$ and

$$\int Q\,dv=0,\qquad \int vQ\,dv=0,\qquad \int |v|^2Q\,dv=0$$

at every $(r,t)$. Suppose pointwise that

$$\partial_tF+v\cdot\nabla_rF+a\cdot\nabla_vF=Q.$$

Define $\rho,u,\Pi,e,q$ as in [[def-csm-dk-kinetic-macroscopic-fields]]. Then the exact balances are

$$\partial_t\rho+\nabla_r\cdot(\rho u)=0,$$

$$\partial_t(\rho u)+\nabla_r\cdot(\rho u\otimes u+\Pi)=\rho a,$$

$$\partial_t\!\left(\frac12\rho|u|^2+e\right)+\nabla_r\cdot\!\left[\left(\frac12\rho|u|^2+e\right)u+\Pi u+q\right]=\rho a\cdot u,$$

and

$$\partial_te+\nabla_r\cdot(eu+q)+\Pi:\nabla_ru=0.$$

These identities are exact moment equations under the stated generic conservation assumptions on $Q$. They do not supply a constitutive relation for $\Pi$ or $q$, a closure, or a hydrodynamic limit.

In the SI physical interpretation, $t$ is measured in seconds, $a$ is acceleration in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$, and $Q$ has the units of $F$ per second.

references.title: R. Fitzpatrick, Plasma Physics, Boltzmann H-Theorem

items.title: Global finite-energy cutoff collision evolution
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Fix a reference speed $v_0>0$, a rate $\lambda>0$, and the weighted space $X=L^1(\mathbb R^3,w_0\,dv)$ with $w_0(v)=1+|v|^2/v_0^2$, as in [[def-csm-dk-reflection-collision-gain]]. Let $f_0\in X$ be nonnegative with $\int f_0\,dv=1$, first moment $m_1=\int vf_0(v)\,dv$, and finite second moment $E_2=\int |v|^2f_0(v)\,dv$. Put

$$K:=\{g\in X:g\ge0\text{ a.e.},\ \int g\,dv=1,\ \int vg\,dv=m_1,\ \int|v|^2g\,dv=E_2\}.$$

Then there is a unique $f\in C([0,\infty),K)$, with continuity in the $X$ norm, satisfying

$$f_t=e^{-\lambda t}f_0+\lambda\int_0^t e^{-\lambda(t-s)}\mathcal G(f_s,f_s)\,ds,$$

where the time integral is the norm limit of Riemann sums in $X$. For all $t\ge0$, $f_t\ge0$, $\int f_t\,dv=1$, $\int vf_t\,dv=\int vf_0\,dv$, and $\int |v|^2f_t\,dv=E_2$. If $f_0>0$ almost everywhere, then $f_t\ge e^{-\lambda t}f_0$ almost everywhere.

If in addition $f_0\in\mathcal M_{u,a,b}$ for some $u\in\mathbb R^3$ and $0<a<b$, with $\mathcal M_{u,a,b}$ as in [[lem-csm-dk-gaussian-mixture-regularity]], then each $f_t$ has a positive $C^\infty$ velocity representative with the Gaussian bounds in that lemma; these representatives depend continuously on $t$ locally uniformly in velocity, are $C^1$ in $t$, and satisfy $\partial_t f_t=\lambda(\mathcal G(f_t,f_t)-f_t)$ pointwise.

references.title: R. Fitzpatrick, Plasma Physics, Boltzmann H-Theorem

items.title: H theorem and Maxwellian equality for the regular cutoff model
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, $v_0>0$, $\lambda>0$, $u\in\mathbb R^3$, and positive velocity-squared parameters $0<a<b$. Let

$$f_0(v)=\tfrac12\gamma_{aI,u}(v)+\tfrac12\gamma_{bI,u}(v),$$

and let $f_t$ be its global solution from [[thm-csm-dk-global-cutoff-collision-evolution]]. Define the dimensionless one-particle functional

$$H(t):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}f_t(v)\log(v_0^3f_t(v))\,dv.$$

For every $t\ge0$, $H$ is finite and continuously differentiable, and with $A=f_t(v)f_t(w)$ and $B=f_t(v')f_t(w')$,

$$H'(t)=-\frac{\lambda}{4}\int_{\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3\times S^2}(B-A)\log(B/A)\,d\mu\le0.$$

The integrand is nonnegative. Equality holds at a time $t$ exactly when $f_t$ is a normalized isotropic Gaussian

$$f_t(v)=(2\pi s^2)^{-3/2}\exp\!\left(-\frac{|v-\bar u|^2}{2s^2}\right)$$

for some $\bar u\in\mathbb R^3$ and $s>0$; every such Gaussian is stationary. The specified initial mixture is not a single Gaussian, so $H'(0)<0$.

references.title: R. Fitzpatrick, Plasma Physics, Boltzmann H-Theorem

items.title: Conditional one-particle kinetic entropy production
items.statement:
Assume the physical adoption [[post-csm-dk-selected-cutoff-kinetic-model]] with a positive collision rate $\lambda$, particle mass $m>0$, reference speed $v_0>0$, and $k_B>0$. Prepare the normalized one-particle velocity density by

$$f_0(v)=\tfrac12\gamma_{aI,u}(v)+\tfrac12\gamma_{bI,u}(v),\qquad u\in\mathbb R^3,\quad 0<a<b,$$

with covariance variances $a,b$ in $(\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}})^2$, where $\gamma_{\Sigma,u}$ is the normalized Gaussian defined in [[lem-csm-dk-gaussian-mixture-regularity]]. For the resulting global regular model solution $f_t$, define the one-particle reference information entropy

$$S_B(t):=-k_B\int_{\mathbb R^3}f_t(v)\log(v_0^3f_t(v))\,dv.$$

Then the model deduction is

$$\frac{dS_B}{dt}=\frac{k_B\lambda}{4}\int_{\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3\times S^2}(B-A)\log(B/A)\,d\mu\ge0,$$

where $A=f_t(v)f_t(w)$ and $B=f_t(v')f_t(w')$ use the exact reflection variables of [[post-csm-dk-selected-cutoff-kinetic-model]]. The derivative is strictly positive at $t=0$. Equality at any time holds exactly for a normalized isotropic Maxwellian velocity density.

This conclusion is conditional on the adopted closed homogeneous model and regular preparation. It identifies a one-particle information functional with entropy units; it does not assert the fine-grained entropy of an $N$-particle ensemble, a general thermodynamic second law, or empirical entropy increase.

references.title: R. Fitzpatrick, Plasma Physics, Boltzmann H-Theorem

items.physical_scope: Conditional prediction of nondecrease of the declared one-particle velocity-reference information entropy for the adopted homogeneous cutoff reflection model and the specified positive regular Gaussian-mixture preparation. It is not a statement about fine-grained N-particle Gibbs entropy, generic gases, a hard-sphere Boltzmann–Grad limit, hydrodynamic limits, experiments, or all physical realizations.

items.title: Equal scalar kinetic fields with unequal covariance stress
items.statement: For solutions in the setting of [[thm-csm-dk-exact-kinetic-moments]], any two velocity densities with the same scalar fields $n$, $u$, and $e$ have the same covariance stress $\Pi$.
